name: Annette Alder
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still have a report that said I sang too quietly for a lead.” People around Juniper Street know Annette by a small Sunday habit. Annette knows which of the west-side porches has a seat in the shade.
voice: I conduct the choir. My instinct was to fill the space and I practiced keeping my hands down.
appearance: Annette has fine brows over wide-set eyes. Look for a cropped cut that shows the shape of the ears. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is an old plum windbreaker with a copper-colored clasp that has been repaired by hand. In conversation Annette listens with the head tilted a little to the left.
personality: Annette admires skill and distrusts the idea that skill gives anyone permission to be rude. Annette learns fastest from somebody willing to show how they made a mistake.
agenda: To teach the choir to hold the silence together.
family: Johan Vega is Annette’s stepsibling. Annette asks before bringing somebody along. Johan can always ask for five minutes alone. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *The new language at dinner*, Johan says, “I can swap two calls and cover one dinner. Somebody needs to count the extra bus fare.”
connections: Bianca Sethi (choir student). The conductor and writer agree who controls the unsung verse.

reactions.situation: The silent verse gets applause in the wrong place
reactions.response: Annette gives the singer time to resume instead of trying to conduct the applause.

reactions.response: Annette puts distance between the frightened person and the argument and asks nearby staff for help.
